title: Experiment with the text before interpreting it
statement: Let students try contrasting readings or change one element of a scene, predict what changes for characters and audience, and explain why, before any finished interpretation is given.
detail: A published teaching pack, chosen as the central reference for the Grade 9 unit's teaching approach, has students explore punctuation through movement, relationships through rhythm and unresolved problems through passing an object between speakers, which makes aspects of the text available for investigation before a finished interpretation is supplied (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, lines 2978 and 3073). The unit's design brief turns this into rehearsal as investigation: students try contrasting readings or staging choices, predict their effects and explain what changed (line 3091). An advanced-learning resource, written after the first plan was found too basic beside the Grade 3 lessons, proposes changing who hears an aside, removing a line or altering a performance choice, then predicting what changes for each character and the audience and defending the causal explanation (lines 2534-2626). That resource was endorsed as the basis for the build (line 2705).
against: Untested with students: both are designs, and the brief adds: "Peer rehearsal remains valuable; an AI response is not an equivalent replacement." (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, line 3091).

evidence.quote: The RSC pack has students explore punctuation through movement, relationships through rhythm, and unresolved problems through passing an object between speakers.
These activities make aspects of the text available for investigation before a finished interpretation is supplied.
Students try contrasting readings or staging choices, predict their effects and explain what changed.
Change who hears an aside, remove a line, or alter a performance choice.
Students predict what changes for each character and the audience, then defend the causal explanation.
